Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed, we want to capture a concise workload profile and a small candidate model shortlist to hand off to implementation. This will help us size Dedicated capacity (if you go that route) and set sensible latency targets for the first-phase rollout.

Could you attach the traffic profile (approx daily active requests, peak qps, typical prompt lengths) and confirm whether the LLM calls will include:
- Long single-document context (>= 8k tokens) vs. several short messages (<= 1k tokens)
- Any synchronous low-latency rules (95th percentile target <= 250ms for token start)
- Data handling constraints (PII redaction requirement, retention < 30 days?)

I’ll pull together a 3-model shortlist tuned to your profile and an initial cost/latency matrix by Friday.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Sr. Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Tessa —

Thanks — attaching the profile you asked for. Quick clarifications inline:
- Traffic: see column "median_daily_calls" and "peak_hour_qps". We anticipate steady growth but first 3 months target is the numbers in rows 1–3.
- Context: primary use case is multi-section clinical note summarization. Typical sequences are ~6–10k tokens (we often pass the whole note as one prompt). We do also have a chat-like triage interface with shorter prompts (~400–800 tokens).
- Latency: we need interactive UX for the triage flow (p50 ~ 200–300ms target). Long-note summarization can be async (batch) with a 30s SLA.
- Data: PHI present in notes. Retention rule: redact and discard request payloads within 7 days; logs must not contain PHI.

Attached: Aurelia_traffic_profile.csv (contains the columns and a short usage projection).

Emily Zhao
Platform Lead, Integrations
Aurelia Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Onboarding: candidate models & expected runtime profile

Thanks for the profile, Emily — good detail. Based on the 6–10k token long-note path + a separate low-latency triage flow, my initial shortlist:

1) small-llama-70b-Q4 (quantized) — best for cost/throughput for long-context summarization when we can batch; expect good summary quality, moderate latency when using batched async routes.
2) long-context-flan2-13b — optimized for 32k token contexts, lower VRAM footprint, faster on Ampere-class GPUs for single-stream long reads.
3) chatlite-7b-optimized — for the triage flow where p50 latency needs to be ~200ms; very low cost per request and supports streaming.

Notes / sizing assumptions:
- For the long-note path, assume average prompt+completion 8k tokens with 80% of traffic handled via batch jobs during off-peak windows. If we target 80% batching, initial Dedicated pool of 4x A100-80GB or equivalent should sustain expected throughput with autoscale headroom.
- For triage flow, provision a small pool of 2x A100-80GB (or equivalent lower-instance types with optimized kernels) to meet p95 targets; prefer model variants with optimized attention kernels.
- We recommend a cache layer for frequent prefix patterns (EHR templates) to cut token spend ~15–25%.

I attached a short PDF with the shortlist rationale + an initial per-token cost model. Happy to tweak once we see their infra constraints.

Ben Carter
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_model_shortlist.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
